html:
A port city on an island off the coast of Kenya, for centuries one of the main Swahili city-states of the East African coast and today the largest port in East Africa.

Its Swahili merchants traded ivory, gold and slaves from the interior for cloth, beads and porcelain brought by monsoon winds from Arabia, India and China. Ibn Battuta stopped there in 1331. In 1498 Vasco da Gama got a hostile welcome and sailed on to its rival Malindi.

The Portuguese sacked Mombasa several times and in 1593 built Fort Jesus to hold it. In 1698, after a siege of nearly three years, Arabs from Oman took the fort. Mombasa was then ruled by Omani governors, the Mazrui, and from 1837 by the sultans of Zanzibar.

Britain made it the capital of its East Africa Protectorate, later British East Africa, in 1895. The Uganda Railway was built inland from Mombasa from 1896, with labourers brought from India. In 1905 the capital moved up the line to Nairobi, a town the railway had created. A new Mombasa to Nairobi railway, built with Chinese loans, opened in 2017.
sum: A port city on an island off the coast of Kenya, for centuries one of the main Swahili city-states of the East African coast and today the largest port in East Africa.
